guides.title: Wix or a custom website? | Little Fight NYC
guides.heading: Should you keep Wix or build a custom website?
guides.summary: Wix can be a sensible home for a simple site. A custom build earns its cost when the website has to carry a specific business job that the current setup makes hard.
guides.description: Compare Wix and a custom website by editing, ownership, integrations, maintenance, and the customer action that matters most.
guides.bodyHtml:
Start with the job, not the platform

A website needs to help someone do something: understand a service, choose a time, call, buy, or find the right location. Wix can do that job well when the business has a small number of pages, straightforward updates, and a person who will keep the information current.

A custom site becomes useful when the business needs a particular workflow, explanation, or presentation that existing tools make awkward. It can also give an owner a clearly documented handoff. Custom code does not earn better Google placement by itself. Clear pages, useful information, and a working customer path matter more.

Put your real work on the table

QuestionWix may fitA custom build may fit
Who changes the site?Someone at the business can comfortably make routine edits.Edits need design or technical care, and you want a defined person responsible.
What must a visitor do?Existing pages and tools present the action clearly and work reliably.The business needs a customer path existing tools cannot present or connect cleanly.
What happens if you leave?You accept rebuilding the site elsewhere later.You want the delivered files and handoff terms written down now.
What needs upkeep?Pages and business details change occasionally.Several connected tools, custom behavior, or ongoing content need a plan.

Choose the route that your business can finish and maintain. A polished custom project still needs the right photos, copy, and approvals.

Make the decision in three steps

  1. Write the customer action. Use one sentence: “A new customer should be able to …” If the sentence is fuzzy, platform shopping will not fix it.
  2. List the people and tools around that action. Include the person who edits the page, booking or payment tools, and where inquiries land.
  3. Ask for the exit plan before the build plan. Ask what you own, where the domain lives, what can be exported, and who can work on it later.
What the owner still decides

Every platform needs accurate service language, useful photographs, a working booking or inquiry path, and current business details. Give those decisions an owner before you spend time redesigning.

Useful facts to verify before moving

Read Wix’s current guidance on exporting content for the parts of your site that matter. Export options differ by feature, so “we can move it later” should become a list: pages, images, blog posts, forms, bookings, contacts, and any paid tool.

For a business that needs a custom site, the useful conversation is about the customer action and ownership. The website service explains how Little Fight scopes that work. Read the WordPress, Webflow, and custom comparison if Wix is only one of several options you are weighing.

guides.title: What a small-business website needs | Little Fight NYC
guides.heading: What should a small-business website include before it launches?
guides.summary: A useful small-business site makes the offer clear, shows why a customer can trust it, and gives that customer a reliable next step.
guides.description: Decide whether to repair or rebuild, prepare the right materials, and understand a custom website project.
guides.bodyHtml:
Build around one customer decision

Start with the decision that keeps the business moving. A salon customer may need to choose a service and book. A contractor’s customer may need to understand the work, see relevant examples, and request a visit. A shop customer may need hours, directions, and a reason to come in.

Every page should support that decision. The home page introduces it. Service pages explain it. A contact or booking path completes it. Pages that do none of those jobs can wait. This keeps the launch focused when the business has more ideas than room on the first version.

Repair or rebuild?

What you findUsually start with
The business details are wrong, pages are confusing, or photos are old.Repair the copy, structure, images, and contact path.
The site works on a computer but fails on a phone.Test the key action on a phone, then fix layout, taps, forms, and reading order.
Inquiries disappear or booking does not match the calendar.Fix the delivery or scheduling path before redesigning the visual layer.
The platform blocks the action the business needs.Plan a rebuild around that specific limitation.

A rebuild is a business decision. It should have a stated reason beyond “the current site looks old.”

Bring the materials that make a site real

  1. Say what you do in plain language. Write the services, who they are for, and what a customer should do next.
  2. Gather proof. Use approved work, real photographs, accurate reviews, licenses, menus, policies, or process details that a customer can check.
  3. List every connected account. Domain, email, forms, analytics, booking, payment, maps, and social profiles belong on one inventory.
  4. Name the approver. A launch moves faster when one person can answer copy and image questions.
What a designer cannot safely guess

Hours, service boundaries, cancellation rules, prices, licensed claims, and what happens after a form is sent all need an owner at the business. Guessing makes a polished site less trustworthy.

What a sound build process looks like

Customer decisionMaterials and accessWorking pagesPhone and form testLaunch

Little Fight builds custom websites with a written scope. A website can be ready in six weeks or less when the scope and materials are agreed. The written plan should say what the business supplies, what gets tested, and what happens after launch. See the Grand Funding project, or use the form delivery guide if inquiries are the immediate problem.

Google’s SEO Starter Guide is a useful check for clear page titles, ordinary links, and information people can use.

guides.title: Website form messages missing? | Little Fight NYC
guides.heading: Why are website form messages not reaching your business?
guides.summary: A thank-you message only proves that the browser showed a result. Follow the request through the form provider, email delivery, inbox, and the person responsible for replying.
guides.description: Test a website form safely, separate browser success from delivery, and prevent lost customer inquiries.
guides.bodyHtml:
Find the missing handoff

Someone can fill out a form, see a thank-you message, and still leave you with no usable inquiry. A website form has several handoffs. The page sends data to a provider or server. That system records or rejects it. A notification travels to a mailbox. Then a person sees it and replies.

Test one handoff at a time. Do not start by rebuilding the whole website.

Browser submitsProvider receivesEmail sendsInbox receivesPerson replies

Run a controlled test

  1. Use a clearly marked test message. Include the date and a phrase you can search for. Do not put passwords, customer details, or card information in it.
  2. Confirm the browser result. Capture the page confirmation and note the exact time. That only confirms the browser-side step.
  3. Check the provider record. Review the form service or server log for the same test. A provider receipt is stronger evidence than a thank-you page.
  4. Check every delivery destination. Look in the intended inbox, spam or quarantine area, and any shared mailbox rules.
  5. Confirm a reply owner. A working form still fails the customer when nobody is watching the inbox.

Use the symptom to narrow the fix

What happenedWhere to look
Every test fails before confirmation.Required fields, browser errors, form configuration, or the endpoint.
The provider records a test but email never arrives.Notification address, email rules, spam or quarantine, and sender setup.
Some inquiries arrive and others do not.Field validation, attachment limits, spam controls, and patterns in the missing messages.
Messages arrive but sit unanswered.Shared inbox access, alerts, coverage, and a named reply owner.
Why a one-time test is not enough

Providers can quarantine a message, a mailbox rule can change, and an email address can be updated later. Keep a short test record after changes and test again after a form, domain, or email provider changes. If you use Netlify Forms, its submission guidance explains that verified and spam submissions are separate views.

Protect the customer path

Use a visible phone or email route as a backup for a high-value action. Keep the confirmation page clear about what happens next. Never ask visitors to send passwords through a contact form. Keep the test record with the form owner.

The IT support service covers the technical investigation when the path is unclear. If booking is the problem, map the calendar paths with the double-booking guide.

guides.title: Own your domain and website accounts | Little Fight NYC
guides.heading: How do you make sure your business owns its domain and website accounts?
guides.summary: Put the domain, recovery email, payment method, and key website accounts under business control. Record who can sign in before an emergency makes the question expensive.
guides.description: Learn which website accounts matter, what a registrar is, and how to document access without breaking live services.
guides.bodyHtml:
Know which account holds what

Your registrar is the company where a domain name is registered and renewed. It may be different from the company that hosts the website or runs business email. One person can build a site while the business still owns every account. That is the cleanest arrangement.

Ownership means the business controls the account email, recovery method, payment method, and permissions. A vendor can receive access without becoming the only person able to recover the account.

Make one ownership record

AccountRecord nowDo not do casually
Domain registrarLogin owner, recovery email, renewal date, and billing owner.Move the domain or edit DNS records during a live outage.
Website host or platformAccount owner, billing owner, administrator access, and support route.Remove a working administrator before another owner can sign in.
Business emailAdmin account, recovery method, mailbox owners, and forwarding rules.Change mail records without knowing which service uses them.
Forms, booking, analytics, and mapsAccount owner, connected email, and who receives alerts.Assume a public profile proves you control its account.

Do this without breaking a working site

  1. Inventory access first. List every account and current owner. Take a careful record of what is connected.
  2. Add a business-controlled recovery route. Use an approved business email and a durable recovery method.
  3. Test the new owner can sign in. Do this before removing or downgrading anyone else.
  4. Store the record safely. Keep account names, renewal dates, and recovery procedures where the business can find them.
  5. Ask before changing technical records. DNS records can control the website, email, and other services at once.
Why DNS needs a pause

DNS directs the domain to services such as the website and email. A change can be correct and still interrupt a live service if it is made without the existing records and a plan. Make a record, choose a maintenance window when possible, and confirm the change with the person responsible.

Use the provider’s transfer rules

Domain moves have provider-specific requirements. Read the ICANN domain holder guidance and your registrar’s current transfer instructions before unlocking or moving anything. The important question is simple: can the business owner recover this account without asking a former employee or vendor?

For a broader website inventory, use the website planning guide. The consulting service is appropriate when the account map is unclear and you need a calm, documented handoff.

guides.title: Move off Squarespace without breaking booking | Little Fight NYC
guides.heading: How do you move off Squarespace without breaking booking?
guides.summary: Treat a platform move as a continuity project. List what stays, what moves, and what needs a live test before you point the domain somewhere new.
guides.description: A safe Squarespace migration checklist for businesses with bookings. Map calendar, notifications, domain settings, forms, and customer links before launch.
guides.bodyHtml:
Protect the appointment path first

A redesign can wait. A booking failure cannot. Before moving a site, write down every route a customer uses to schedule: buttons on the site, links in email, links on social profiles, QR codes, Google Business Profile, and staff messages. Then identify which calendar is the real source of availability.

Many businesses keep the same booking provider during a website move. That can make the first launch safer because the calendar, customer records, and confirmation messages keep their existing home.

Sort each piece of the old site

PieceStaysMovesMust be tested
Domain nameIt can stay at its current registrar.Only move it when account ownership is clear.Website and email records after any DNS change.
Booking calendarKeep the existing provider when it works.Move only with a customer and data plan.Availability, confirmation, reminder, cancellation, and staff view.
Pages and imagesKeep the facts and approved media.Rebuild the pages for the new system.Links, search titles, and contact details.
Forms and notificationsKeep the business inbox.Replace the form setup.Provider receipt, inbox delivery, and reply coverage.

Use a controlled launch sequence

  1. Build and review away from the live domain. Check content, mobile layout, and the primary booking action before launch day.
  2. Run a test appointment under the provider’s rules. Confirm availability, confirmation, reminders, staff visibility, and cancellation. Cancel the test cleanly.
  3. Test the contact path. A browser thank-you message is only the first signal. Confirm the provider, inbox, and human reply path.
  4. Point the domain only after the test list passes. Keep a record of current DNS settings before editing.
  5. Check every public route after launch. Test the main button, old booking links, Google profile, and a phone-sized screen.
What to tell returning customers

Keep the booking wording familiar during the move. If the customer uses the same calendar, say so. If anything changes, explain the action in one sentence and keep the old link redirected or updated where possible.

Read the platform rules before exporting

Squarespace documents its current site export limits. Some content and features will need a planned rebuild, so export is a record of content rather than a promise that a new site will be identical.

Use the double-booking guide to map calendar ownership. The form guide covers the second common failure point. A custom website scope should name the test plan and handoff before the domain changes.

guides.title: How to stop double bookings | Little Fight NYC
guides.heading: How do you stop double bookings without making customers work harder?
guides.summary: Double bookings happen when more than one place can promise the same time. Choose one calendar to control availability, then map every path that feeds it.
guides.description: Map booking entry points, choose one source of truth, and test changes safely before customers use them.
guides.bodyHtml:
Choose the calendar that gets the final say

A double booking is usually a system problem, not a staff mistake. It happens when two calendars can each offer the same slot, or when a booking tool does not receive a change quickly enough.

Pick one calendar as the source of truth. That is the place where availability is created, blocked, and confirmed. Every other tool should either read from it or send changes to it in a way you can test.

Customer linksBooking toolAvailability calendarStaff viewCustomer confirmation

Map every promise a customer can see

  1. Collect every booking link. Include the website, Google profile, social bio, reminders, staff messages, QR codes, and marketplace listings.
  2. Write down every calendar. Include personal calendars, room calendars, staff scheduling tools, and paper or spreadsheet workarounds.
  3. Mark the source of truth. One calendar should decide whether a time is available.
  4. Check how changes travel. A reschedule, cancellation, and staff block should reach every needed view.
  5. Run one controlled test. Make, reschedule, and cancel a test booking in a safe time slot. Confirm the customer and staff views agree.

Find the pattern before changing tools

PatternLikely gapFirst check
Two customers get the same time.Separate availability sources or delayed sync.Which calendar accepted each booking?
Staff blocks do not appear online.Personal or staff calendar is outside the booking system.Whether the block is connected to the source of truth.
Cancelled slots keep appearing unavailable.Cancellation is not completing in every system.Booking provider history and calendar event status.
Customers book the wrong service or person.The service menu or staff rules are unclear.What the booking screen promises before checkout.
Why two booking tools are hard to manage

Two tools can work when their ownership, sync direction, and failure plan are documented. They create risk when staff are expected to remember which one wins during a busy day.

Make the public path match the real one

Use the same booking destination on the website, Google profile, social bio, and printed materials where practical. A customer should not have to guess which link is current. Keep clear confirmation and cancellation instructions at the point of booking.

If Google Calendar runs the bookings, its appointment schedule guidance explains how a booking page checks availability and blocks conflicts. Other providers have their own rules, so use their current documentation before changing a sync.

The Squarespace migration guide shows how this map protects a platform move. If the broken path includes website inquiries rather than appointments, use the form delivery guide. Little Fight can review a booking system as part of tech consulting when the current setup is unclear.

guides.title: WordPress, Webflow, or custom? | Little Fight NYC
guides.heading: Should your business use WordPress, Webflow, or a custom website?
guides.summary: All three can support a serious business. The durable choice depends on who will update the site, what the customer needs to do, and how much control the business needs after launch.
guides.description: Compare WordPress, Webflow, and custom sites by maintenance, editing, platform dependence, and ownership.
guides.bodyHtml:
Pick for year two

The build is a short part of a website’s life. The harder question is who handles a new service, an outdated page, a broken integration, or a staff change next year. Put a real name beside that work before choosing a platform.

Each option can be right. Little Fight builds custom sites, so that bias should be clear. A business that publishes constantly or needs an existing platform feature may have a better fit elsewhere.

Compare the ongoing job

OptionGood fit whenOwner needs to plan for
WordPressYou publish substantial content or need a mature publishing system.Core, theme, plugin, hosting, backup, and access responsibilities.
WebflowDesign control and a hosted editor suit the people maintaining it.Platform account ownership, editor training, and the practical cost of moving later.
CustomThe site has a clear customer job and changes are planned rather than constant.A documented relationship for updates, integrations, and handoff.

Custom does not mean untouched. It means the maintenance plan is matched to the small number of parts the site actually uses.

Ask these questions before you sign

  1. How often will we honestly edit the site? Count normal changes over a year, not the changes you hope to make.
  2. Who owns the accounts? The business should control the domain, billing, recovery routes, and access record.
  3. Which integrations carry customer information or money? Booking, payments, forms, email, and analytics need named owners and test plans.
  4. What breaks first? Ask for the support route, update work, and recovery process in writing.
  5. What can we take with us? Ask what exports cleanly and what must be rebuilt.
Platform guidance changes

Read the current official documentation for the version and plan you are considering. WordPress, Webflow, and hosting providers change features and terms. A builder should explain the decision in business language before relying on a technical feature list.

Make the tradeoff visible

WordPress has a large ecosystem, and its own update guidance makes clear that updates are an operating task. Webflow documents what can be exported as site code; connected CMS, ecommerce, and hosting behavior need their own review. A custom site should come with equally clear information about the delivered files and later changes.

Read the Wix comparison for the platform-versus-custom question, and the ownership guide before moving any domain or account. A website scope should make the long-term responsibility clear before work starts.

guides.title: What Google looks for on a business website | Little Fight NYC
guides.heading: What does Google look for on a business website?
guides.summary: Give customers clear answers, keep the business facts accurate, and make important pages available through ordinary links. Search visibility follows useful work over time; it is not a switch a designer can flip.
guides.description: Learn how useful pages, accurate business information, internal links, and original evidence help Google understand a site.
guides.bodyHtml:
Make the business easy to understand

Google needs a page it can find and understand. Customers need the same thing. A useful page names the service, explains who it is for, answers the question that brought the person there, and gives them a clear next step.

That is different from making a page for every phrase someone might type. One strong guide can answer several related questions when it gives a real explanation, an example, and links to the next useful page.

Turn one real question into a useful page

Customer questionDirect answerEvidence and stepsRelated pageAccurate contact path

For example, “Are form messages reaching us?” should lead to a page that shows how to test the full delivery path. The form guide does that by separating browser confirmation, provider receipt, inbox delivery, and a human reply. That is more useful than repeating “we build websites” under several headings.

Keep these basics accurate

Part of the siteWhat to check
Service pagesThey explain a real service, audience, and next action in plain words.
Business factsName, phone, hours, service area, and public profiles agree where they should.
LinksImportant pages can be reached through ordinary links, not only a search box or visual effect.
Images and examplesThey support the page’s subject and use meaningful text alternatives when needed.
Technical healthPages load, work on a phone, and do not hide the primary answer behind a failed interaction.

Use search guidance as a quality check

  1. Read the page as a customer. Can a person tell what this is and whether it helps?
  2. Check the evidence. Replace claims that cannot be shown with a specific process, source, or useful instruction.
  3. Link the next decision. A guide about booking should link to booking or form help, not a pile of unrelated pages.
  4. Keep the information current. Review hours, services, contact paths, and changing platform guidance.
What structured data and AI tools cannot promise

Structured data can help systems read information, but it does not guarantee a special result. An AI answer or a search citation is not a booked project. Measure inquiries that arrive and conversations that become useful work.

Use primary guidance for changing rules

Google’s helpful content guidance emphasizes people-first, original content. Its SEO Starter Guide covers the durable basics. Google Business Profile visibility also depends on relevance, distance, and prominence, as Google explains in its local ranking guidance.

Use the Google Maps guide for a local listing problem. The website service is for the work of making the customer path and the underlying pages clear.
